accessibility.title: Accessible Cary Plastic Surgery Website
accessibility.description: Explore Cary Plastic Surgery’s accessible website designed for all, including the visually impaired.

blocks.text:
**General**
Cary Plastic Surgery strongly believes that every person has the right to live with dignity, equality, comfort, and independence and strives to ensure that our services are accessible to people with disabilities. Toward that goal, we have invested resources to make our website https://caryplasticsurgery.com easier to use and more accessible for people with disabilities.

**Accessibility**
Cary Plastic Surgery has taken great care to ensure our website has been built to be accessible to those who may be visually impaired or require a screen reader to access our website. We utilize several accessibility auditing tools such as “[Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview/)” and “[Axe](https://www.deque.com/axe/)” to accomplish this. These accessibility tools allow our website to improve its compliance by conforming with the World Wide Web Consortium’s (W3C) Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 level AA success criteria.

**Disclaimer**
Cary Plastic Surgery continues efforts to improve the accessibility of our website and services to facilitate accessibility and ease of use for all persons, including those with disabilities. Despite our best efforts to make all pages and content on our website fully accessible, some content may not yet be fully adapted to the strictest accessibility standards. This may be a result of not having found or identified the most appropriate technological solution.

**Third-Party Websites**
Below are the Accessibility Policies provided from the following third-party websites, which are publicly available:

items: [Facebook Accessibility Policy](https://www.facebook.com/help/accessibility)
[Instagram Accessibility Announcement](https://9to5mac.com/2018/11/28/accessibility-instagram-alternative-text/)
[Instagram Accessibility](https://help.instagram.com/1178723545597542)
[Twitter Accessibility](https://help.twitter.com/en/using-twitter/picture-descriptions)
[YouTube Accessibility Policy](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/189278?hl=en)

blocks.text:
**Report Accessibility-Related Issue**
Cary Plastic Surgery takes website accessibility seriously and appreciates your feedback. If you are experiencing accessibility issues on our website, please submit an email to: webmaster@infostarproductions.com. Please provide us with as many specific details as possible regarding your accessibility issue so we may address your concerns. Thank you.

blocks.text: Arm lift surgery, or brachioplasty, removes excess skin and fat from the upper arms while tightening underlying tissues to create a more contoured and toned appearance. This procedure is ideal for individuals experiencing sagging or loose arm skin due to significant weight loss, aging, or genetics, and it focuses on achieving natural, proportionate results that enhance overall arm aesthetics and mobility, often leading to greater self-assurance based on insights from thousands of patients over the years.
**Key Benefits**

items: Eliminated sagging skin for firmer, more defined upper arms.
Enhanced comfort and range of motion by reducing excess tissue.
Boosted confidence in clothing choices and daily activities through refined contours.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Consultations involve a thorough assessment of arm skin elasticity, fat distribution, and goals, often using imaging to visualize potential outcomes. The surgery typically lasts two to three hours under general anesthesia, with incisions placed discreetly to excise tissue and tighten structures. Recovery allows a return to light activities within one to two weeks, with swelling and bruising gradually resolving over several weeks to months as final shapes emerge. Costs start around $7,000 to $10,000, varying based on the extent of correction and any combined procedures.

*As a board-certified plastic surgeon with decades of experience at Cary Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I have performed arm lifts on thousands of patients, earning multiple "Voted Best Plastic Surgery" awards in the area. This procedure is particularly empowering for those dealing with "bat wings" or loose arm skin after weight loss or aging, helping restore a sleek, youthful profile that complements their lifestyle and boosts daily comfort. Essential concerns I prioritize based on patient outcomes include ensuring weight stability pre-surgery to maintain contours, using advanced scar-minimizing techniques, and providing detailed guidance on post-op arm exercises to support muscle tone and healing.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With over thirty years of expertise and thousands of arm lifts performed, I have mastered techniques that deliver natural, toned arms without compromising mobility, focusing on precise tissue removal and scar concealment.

Patients often share how this surgery freed them to wear sleeveless outfits confidently after years of hiding loose skin. As a repeated award-winner for Best Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I prioritize your specific concerns like post-weight loss sagging or genetic laxity to ensure customized plans that may include liposuction for added refinement and long-term satisfaction.
Benefits of Arm Lift Surgery
From my experience, an arm lift revitalizes more than appearance—it's about reclaiming ease and poise in movement. Key benefits include:

items: Tightened contours for sleeker, more youthful upper arms.
Reduced excess skin that causes chafing or discomfort during activities.
Better arm symmetry and proportion to enhance overall body harmony.
Improved fit in clothing, allowing greater style versatility.
Elevated self-esteem; patients frequently report feeling more active and assured.
Long-term advantages are supported by healthy habits, preserving the refined shape over time.

blocks.text: Visit the [American Society of Plastic Surgeons website](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/cosmetic-procedures/arm-lift) for complete information on arm lift surgery.
Ideal Candidates
Ideal candidates are healthy adults with excess arm skin or fat that affects their comfort or confidence, often after weight loss or due to aging. Success is highest in those with:

items: Moderate to severe sagging that resists exercise or toning.
Stable weight and good overall health; non-smokers preferred for optimal healing.
Realistic goals for natural enhancement rather than perfection.
You should be free from certain medical conditions impacting recovery. If fat is the main issue without much skin laxity, liposuction alone may be suitable.

blocks.text: [Schedule a Consultation](/request-appointment) to find out if you're a candidate.
Technique Options

rows: Incision from underarm to elbow; removes excess skin/fat, tightens tissues. Scarring fades well along the inner arm.
Shorter incision in underarm; focuses on upper arm laxity. Recovery time is short with minimal, hidden scarring.
Incision extends to chest; addresses side/arm excess for full contour including flanks. Scarring is concealable.
Massive weight loss with widespread laxity.
Adds fat suction via cannula for a smoother, defined result.

blocks.text: Arm Lift Surgery, Step-by-Step
The surgery takes place in our accredited facility under general anesthesia, lasting two to three hours. Steps include:

items:
**Incision:**
Placed along the inner arm for discretion.

**Tissue Removal:**
Excise excess skin and fat; use liposuction if combined.

**Tightening:**
Reshape underlying tissues for support.

**Closure:**
Layered sutures; apply dressings or garments.

blocks.text: You return home the same day with post-care instructions.
Recovery & Aftercare
Recovery emphasizes gentle care and gradual mobility with most patients able to resume light activities in one to two weeks and full routines in four to six weeks. Based on my protocols:

items: **Week 1:** Rest arms elevated to reduce swelling; manage discomfort with meds, avoid lifting.
**Weeks 2-4:** Wear compression sleeves for support; return to desk work, limit arm strain.
**Month 1 and beyond:** Introduce light exercises; monitor scars with moisturizers.

blocks.text:
**Recovery Tips:**
Arrange assistance for tasks, stay hydrated, quit smoking pre/post-op. Long-term: Maintain weight and incorporate arm toning for sustained firmness; annual checks advised.
Risks & Complications
As with any surgery, risks exist but are minimized through expertise. Common risks include swelling, bruising, and temporary numbness. More rare risks may involve infection or asymmetry.
We review your medical history and discuss all possibilities during arm lift surgery to mitigate risks.

Benefits typically outweigh risks for well-suited candidates, with informed consent ensuring peace of mind.
**** Individual results vary**
Cost & Financing

We will always provide transparent pricing with no hidden costs. Arm lift surgery typically starts at $7,000 and includes anesthesia, facility time, and follow-ups. Pricing varies depending on the techniques required and combinations with other surgeries such as a liposuction.
We offer financing through CareCredit and accept major cards. During consultation, get a custom quote; insurance may cover if medically necessary.
[Schedule a consultation](/request-appointment) and we'll provide you with a personalized quote for an arm lift.
Frequently Asked Questions

items: **How long does arm lift surgery take?** About two to three hours at our practice, depending on extent and combinations.
**Will arm lift leave visible scars?** Scars are along the inner arm but fade over six to twelve months; treatments available.
**Can I combine arm lift with other procedures?** Yes, often with liposuction or body lifts for harmony.
**How long do the results of arm lift last?** Results endure many years with stable weight; habits maintain them.
**What if I gain weight after arm lift surgery?** It may affect contours; healthy living advised for longevity.

header.h1: Labial Reduction / Reconstruction in Cary, NC
header.sub: Personalized Care for Comfort, Proportion, and Repair
bullets: Reduce tissue that causes persistent pulling, chafing, or irritation
Repair labial tissue affected by childbirth, injury, or previous surgery
Private, individualized planning with a board-certified plastic surgeon

blocks.text: Labial reduction, commonly called labiaplasty, reshapes or reduces labial tissue. Labial reconstruction repairs or restores tissue changed by childbirth, injury, congenital differences, or previous surgery. Treatment most often involves the labia minora, although the labia majora may also be addressed when appropriate. The goal is a comfortable, proportionate result that respects sensation, function, and your individual anatomy.

Labia naturally vary widely in size, shape, color, and symmetry, and a difference in appearance does not by itself mean that treatment is needed. Some adults consider surgery because tissue twists, pulls, or chafes during exercise, fitted clothing, or intimacy. Others seek reconstruction after tissue has been stretched, torn, or altered. A private consultation is the right setting to discuss what is normal, what is causing symptoms, and whether surgery or a nonsurgical approach best fits your goals.
**Key Benefits**

items: Reduced pulling, pinching, chafing, or irritation during exercise and daily activities.
Repair of tissue changed by childbirth, injury, congenital differences, or previous surgery.
A more balanced, individualized contour planned to preserve healthy tissue and function.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Dr. Hanna will review your health history, symptoms, anatomy, expectations, and plans that could affect the result, including future pregnancy. A straightforward reduction is usually an outpatient procedure that takes about one to two hours; reconstruction may take longer depending on complexity. Many patients return to nonstrenuous work within several days to two weeks, while strenuous exercise, cycling, swimming, tampon use, and sexual activity are generally restricted for four to six weeks. Costs typically range from $5,000 to $8,000, depending on the extent of treatment, anesthesia, facility time, and whether reconstructive repair is required.

*Every patient brings different anatomy, symptoms, and reasons for considering labial surgery. I begin with a private, respectful conversation and an examination focused on what is bothering you. My goal is to recommend only the degree of reduction or reconstruction that can support comfort and proportion while preserving healthy tissue and function.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With more than 30 years of surgical experience and board certification in plastic surgery, I approach intimate procedures with discretion, careful planning, and attention to both form and function. I provide a private, professional setting where you can discuss symptoms, appearance, scarring, sensation, and recovery openly and without pressure.

As a multiple award-winner for Best Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I tailor every surgical plan to the patient's anatomy rather than a single standard of appearance. I consider tissue quality, asymmetry, prior childbirth or surgery, and the amount of correction that can be performed safely, with surgery in an accredited facility and continued follow-up throughout healing.
Potential Benefits & Ideal Candidates
Benefits depend on the reason for surgery and the amount of correction that is appropriate. For a carefully selected adult patient, labial reduction or reconstruction may:

items: Reduce persistent pulling, pinching, chafing, or irritation during exercise and daily activities.
Improve comfort in fitted clothing or during intimacy when excess or damaged tissue is the source of symptoms.
Repair tissue altered by childbirth, injury, congenital differences, or a prior procedure.
Address pronounced asymmetry while preserving a natural, individualized contour.

blocks.text: Ideal Candidates
Candidacy is based on your health, symptoms, anatomy, and expectations, not on a single measurement or idealized appearance. Appropriate candidates are adults who:

items: Have persistent physical discomfort or a reconstructive concern directly related to labial tissue.
Are in good general health, do not smoke, and can follow activity restrictions during healing.
Understand the normal range of labial anatomy and have personal, realistic goals free from outside pressure.
Understand that scarring, altered sensation, asymmetry, and the need for revision are possible.

blocks.text: Read more about informed decision-making from the [American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/vaginal-rejuvenation-labiaplasty-and-other-female-genital-cosmetic-surgery), then [schedule a consultation](/request-appointment) for an individual evaluation.
Technique Options

rows: Removes a measured amount of tissue along the outer edge, then closes the new border with fine absorbable sutures.
Excess tissue distributed along the labial edge or a preference to remove an irregular or darkened border.
Removes a small wedge from the thickest portion and brings the remaining edges together, preserving much of the natural outer border.
Central fullness when retaining the natural edge and pigmentation is a priority.
Repositions or repairs tissue using a plan based on the specific defect. More complex reconstruction may require local tissue rearrangement.
Tissue changes after childbirth, injury, congenital differences, previous surgery, or excessive prior reduction.

blocks.text: Labial Surgery, Step-by-Step

Labial reduction is usually an outpatient procedure. A straightforward reduction often takes about one to two hours; reconstruction may take longer depending on complexity. Your individual plan may include:

items:
**Planning:**
Confirm the treatment area and mark the amount of tissue to be reshaped while you are awake.

**Anesthesia:**
Use local anesthesia with sedation or general anesthesia based on the planned procedure and your needs.

**Reduction or Repair:**
Carefully remove, reshape, or reposition tissue using the selected technique.

**Closure:**
Close the incisions with fine, usually absorbable sutures and provide detailed wound-care instructions.

blocks.text: Recovery & Aftercare

Swelling, bruising, tenderness, and minor spotting are expected early in recovery. Many patients return to nonstrenuous work after several days to two weeks, depending on their procedure and job. Wear loose clothing, keep the area clean as directed, and use cold packs only according to your postoperative instructions.

Strenuous exercise, cycling, swimming, tampon use, and sexual activity are generally restricted for four to six weeks or until Dr. Hanna clears you. Most swelling improves by about six weeks, but subtle swelling can take four to six months to resolve. Your follow-up plan takes priority over any general timeline.
Risks & Complications

Labial surgery has risks, and high-quality long-term evidence for elective cosmetic genital procedures is limited. Possible complications include bleeding or hematoma, infection, delayed healing or wound separation, visible or tender scarring, asymmetry, removing too much or too little tissue, persistent pain, pain with intimacy, altered or reduced sensation, and the need for revision surgery. Anesthesia and blood-clot risks also apply.

Careful examination, conservative planning, smoking cessation, and following postoperative restrictions can reduce risk but cannot eliminate it. Dr. Hanna will review the risks that apply to your anatomy and proposed procedure during informed consent.
**Individual results vary.**
Cost & Financing

We will always provide transparent pricing with no hidden costs. Labial reduction typically starts at $5,000 and includes anesthesia, facility time, and follow-up care. Total costs commonly range from $5,000 to $8,000, depending on the extent of treatment and whether repair of prior injury or surgery is required.

Surgery performed only to change appearance is generally self-pay. Insurance may consider some reconstructive or symptom-driven procedures, but coverage depends on your plan, medical documentation, and prior authorization; it cannot be guaranteed. Financing through CareCredit and major-card payment options are available.
[Schedule a consultation](/request-appointment) to receive an individualized treatment plan and quote.
Frequently Asked Questions

items: **What is the difference between labial reduction and reconstruction?** Reduction removes and reshapes a measured amount of excess tissue. Reconstruction repairs or restores tissue changed by childbirth, injury, congenital differences, previous surgery, or excessive prior reduction. Some procedures involve both.

**How do I know whether my anatomy is normal?** Labia have a very wide normal range of size, shape, color, and symmetry. There is no single ideal measurement. A consultation can determine whether your concern is a normal variation, whether tissue is causing symptoms, and whether treatment is appropriate.

**Will there be visible scars?** Incisions are placed within natural folds and scars often soften over time, but no surgeon can promise an invisible scar. Scar location and length depend on the technique and amount of repair.

**Will surgery change sensation or sexual function?** The plan is designed to preserve healthy tissue and function, but temporary or lasting sensation changes and pain with intimacy are recognized risks. Evidence does not support promising improved sexual function from elective cosmetic surgery.

**When can I exercise or resume sexual activity?** Most patients avoid strenuous exercise, cycling, swimming, tampon use, and sexual activity for about four to six weeks. Resume these activities only after Dr. Hanna examines your healing and clears you.

**Can pregnancy or childbirth affect the result?** Yes. Pregnancy, vaginal delivery, aging, and major weight changes may stretch or alter tissue after surgery. If pregnancy is planned soon, Dr. Hanna may recommend postponing elective treatment.

**Does insurance cover labial surgery?** Cosmetic reduction is usually not covered. A reconstructive procedure or surgery for documented persistent symptoms may be considered by some plans, but coverage and preauthorization requirements vary.

blocks.text: Liposuction, or lipoplasty, is a body contouring procedure that uses a cannula to suction out excess fat deposits from specific areas, refining the body's shape without serving as a weight loss method. This procedure is ideal for individuals with localized fat pockets due to genetics, aging, or post-pregnancy changes that persist despite healthy habits, and it focuses on achieving natural, balanced results that improve overall proportions and confidence, drawing from insights gained through thousands of patients over the years.
**Key Benefits**

items: Eliminated stubborn fat in areas like the abdomen, thighs, hips, arms, or neck for a sleeker profile.
Improved body symmetry and clothing fit through precise sculpting.
Boosted self-assurance in appearance and activities with subtle enhancements.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Consultations involve a detailed review of your body contours, medical history, and goals, often incorporating imaging to simulate outcomes. The surgery typically lasts one to three hours under general anesthesia or sedation, with small incisions allowing fat removal via a cannula. Recovery allows a return to light activities within one to two weeks, with swelling and bruising gradually resolving over several weeks to months as final shapes emerge. Costs start around $5,000 to $9,000, varying based on the number of areas treated and any combined procedures.

*As a board-certified plastic surgeon with decades of experience at Cary Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I have performed liposuction on thousands of patients, earning multiple "Voted Best Plastic Surgery" awards in the area. This procedure is especially valuable for those frustrated by persistent fat despite dedicated fitness and nutrition, often helping reveal underlying muscle definition and restoring proportions lost to life changes. Important aspects I highlight based on patient outcomes include using advanced techniques to minimize irregularities, providing guidance on compression wear for smoother healing, and addressing functional benefits like reduced chafing in treated areas.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With over thirty years in plastic surgery and thousands of liposuction procedures performed, I have refined techniques that deliver smooth, even contours while preserving skin integrity and minimizing downtime.

Patients often express delight at finally achieving the shape their efforts deserve, free from stubborn bulges. As a multiple award-winner for Best Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I emphasize your unique body composition, from fat distribution to skin elasticity, ensuring personalized plans that may integrate with other treatments for holistic enhancement and enduring satisfaction.
Benefits of Liposuction
From my experience, liposuction refines the body in ways that empower patients to embrace their form fully. Key benefits include:

items: Precise fat reduction in targeted areas like the abdomen, thighs, arms, or neck for a more defined silhouette.
Smoother transitions between body regions, enhancing overall proportions.
Reduced discomfort from chafing or rubbing in treated zones for greater daily ease.
Complement to fitness routines by revealing muscle tone hidden under fat layers.
Heightened confidence in clothing and activities; many patients feel more active and stylish.
Long-term advantages are realized with stable habits, sustaining the sculpted results over time.

blocks.text: Visit the [American Society of Plastic Surgeons website](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/cosmetic-procedures/liposuction) for complete information on Liposuction.
Ideal Candidates
Ideal candidates are healthy adults near their target weight with localized fat deposits that resist lifestyle changes, seeking refined contours. Success is highest in those with:

items: Good skin elasticity to allow smooth retraction post-fat removal.
Stable weight and commitment to maintaining it for lasting outcomes.
No significant medical conditions affecting healing; non-smokers preferred.
You should have realistic expectations for sculpting rather than major weight reduction. If skin laxity is prominent, we may recommend combining with procedures like a tummy tuck.

blocks.text: [Schedule a Consultation](/request-appointment) to find out if you're a candidate.
Technique Options

rows: Injects fluid to swell fat; suctions via cannula. Very tiny incisions lead to minimal scaring.
General fat reduction in multiple areas.
Uses laser to liquefy fat before suction. Scars are small and fade - often not noticeable.
Employs sound waves to emulsify fat with minimal scarring.
Vibrating cannula for efficient fat breakdown. Scars are small and fade over time.

blocks.text: Liposuction, Step-by-Step

items:
**Incision:**
Small openings placed discreetly in treatment areas.

**Preperation:**
Inject tumescent solution to ease fat removal and minimize bleeding.

**Fat Removal:**
Insert cannula to break up and suction fat deposits.

**Refinement:**
Sculpt for smooth contours; use energy devices if chosen.

**Closure:**
Close incisions with sutures; apply compression garments.

blocks.text: You return home the same day with post-care instructions.

**Weeks 2-4:** Return to desk work; incorporate light walking, avoid strenuous efforts.
**Month 1 and beyond:** Gradually resume exercise; massage areas to aid smoothness

blocks.text:

Stay hydrated, follow a balanced diet, use scar creams early. Long-term: Regular activity preserves your refined shape; annual visits recommended.

We review your medical history and discuss all possibilities during liposuction to mitigate risks.

Benefits typically outweigh risks for well-suited candidates, with informed consent ensuring peace of mind.

blocks.text: Gynecomastia is the overdevelopment or enlargement of male breast tissue. It may affect one or both sides of the chest and can involve excess glandular tissue, localized fat, stretched skin, or a combination of these concerns. Male breast reduction surgery removes and reshapes this tissue to create a flatter, more proportionate chest contour.

Hormonal changes, heredity, weight changes, certain medications, medical conditions, and substances such as anabolic steroids can contribute to chest enlargement. Fat-dominant pseudogynecomastia is not the same as glandular gynecomastia, so a careful evaluation is important before choosing surgery. When appropriate, Dr. Hanna may recommend medical testing or evaluation of an underlying cause before developing a surgical plan.
**Key Benefits**

items: A flatter, firmer chest contour with improved proportion.
Reduction of excess fat, glandular tissue, and loose skin when needed.
Greater comfort and confidence in fitted clothing, exercise, and daily activities.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Consultation includes a review of your health history, medications and supplements, possible contributing factors, and the balance of fat, glandular tissue, and skin. Surgery is usually an outpatient procedure lasting about one to three hours under general anesthesia or intravenous sedation. Many patients return to desk work and light activities in one to two weeks, while strenuous exercise and heavy upper-body activity are restricted for approximately four to six weeks. Costs typically range from $6,000 to $10,000, depending on whether treatment requires liposuction, gland excision, skin removal, or a combination.

*As a board-certified plastic surgeon with decades of breast and body-contouring experience at Cary Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I understand that gynecomastia can affect comfort, clothing choices, exercise, and confidence. I begin by determining whether fullness comes from fat, glandular tissue, loose skin, or a combination, then tailor the operation to create a natural masculine contour while keeping scars as discreet as the anatomy allows. I evaluate chest shape, skin elasticity, nipple and areola position, asymmetry, and the relative amounts of fat and glandular tissue before recommending a technique.

As a multiple award-winner for Best Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I focus on results that look balanced and natural rather than overcorrected. I explain incision placement, scar tradeoffs, recovery, and the factors that may affect long-term results so each patient can make an informed decision and receive a plan suited to his anatomy.
Benefits of Gynecomastia Surgery
Male breast reduction is designed to improve chest proportion by treating the tissue responsible for persistent fullness. Potential benefits include:

items: A flatter, firmer, and more masculine chest contour.
Removal of glandular tissue that does not respond to diet or exercise.
Reduction of localized chest fat through liposuction when appropriate.
Improved nipple and areola position or stretched skin in more advanced cases.
Greater comfort during exercise and more confidence in fitted shirts or swimwear.

blocks.text: Visit the [American Society of Plastic Surgeons website](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/cosmetic-procedures/gynecomastia-surgery) for additional information about gynecomastia surgery.

items: Have persistent glandular tissue, localized fat, loose skin, or asymmetry that causes concern.
Be at a relatively stable weight and understand that surgery is not a substitute for weight loss.
Be nonsmokers or willing to stop smoking as directed before and after surgery.
Have realistic expectations about scars, symmetry, sensation, and the time required for swelling to resolve.
Have possible medication, hormonal, substance-related, or medical causes evaluated before elective treatment.

blocks.text: Adolescents may sometimes be considered when development is stable and symptoms persist, but continued breast development can create a need for future treatment. rows: Removes localized fatty tissue through several small incisions using a thin cannula. Liposuction does not remove firm glandular tissue.
Fat-dominant fullness with good skin elasticity.
Removes dense glandular tissue through an incision commonly placed along part of the areola border.

Uses liposuction to refine fatty areas and direct excision to remove glandular tissue and shape the chest.
Removes excess skin and may reduce or reposition the areola when significant enlargement has stretched the tissues.
More advanced gynecomastia with sagging skin or an enlarged, low areola.

blocks.text: Gynecomastia Surgery, Step-by-Step
Gynecomastia surgery is usually performed as an outpatient procedure under general anesthesia or intravenous sedation and commonly lasts one to three hours. Your procedure may include:

items: **Anesthesia:** Medication is administered for comfort based on the procedure and your health.
**Incisions:** Small liposuction access points or discreet incisions near the areola are planned according to the tissue being treated.
**Fat and Gland Removal:** Excess fat is reduced with liposuction, firm glandular tissue is excised, or both techniques are combined.
**Contour Refinement:** The chest is shaped for symmetry; excess skin or the areola is adjusted when necessary.
**Closure and Support:** Incisions are closed, dressings and a compression garment are applied, and temporary drains may be used in some cases.

blocks.text: You will usually return home the same day with detailed aftercare instructions and scheduled follow-up.
Recovery & Aftercare

Soreness, bruising, tightness, and swelling are expected early in recovery. Many patients return to desk work within one to two weeks, while heavy lifting, chest workouts, and strenuous activity are restricted for approximately four to six weeks or until Dr. Hanna clears them.

items: **First several days:** Rest, walk periodically, take medication as directed, and protect the incisions and any drains.
**Weeks 1–2:** Continue wearing the prescribed compression garment and gradually resume light daily activities.
**Weeks 3–6:** Increase activity only as directed and avoid pressure, heavy lifting, and upper-body exercise until cleared.
**Months 3–6:** Residual swelling continues to resolve and the chest contour becomes more defined; scars continue fading over time.

blocks.text: Maintain a stable weight, avoid nicotine, attend follow-up visits, and contact the office for increasing pain, spreading redness, fever, shortness of breath, chest pain, or an unusual heartbeat.
Risks & Complications

Gynecomastia surgery carries risks including bleeding or hematoma, infection, fluid accumulation, poor wound healing, contour irregularities, asymmetry, persistent pain, fat necrosis, and temporary or permanent changes in nipple or chest sensation. Scars are permanent, although they typically fade, and additional surgery may be needed to address a complication or refine the result.

Anesthesia, blood-clot, cardiac, and pulmonary risks also apply. A complete health history, evaluation of possible underlying causes, smoking cessation, and careful adherence to postoperative instructions can reduce risk but cannot eliminate it. Dr. Hanna will review the risks relevant to your health and surgical plan during informed consent.
**Individual results vary.**
Cost & Financing

We will always provide transparent pricing with no hidden costs. Gynecomastia surgery typically starts around $6,000 and includes anesthesia, facility time, and follow-up care. Total costs commonly range from $6,000 to $10,000, depending on whether treatment requires liposuction, gland excision, skin removal, or a combination.

Most health plans consider male breast reduction cosmetic, although coverage varies and may be considered in some medically documented cases. Financing through CareCredit and major-card payment options are available. A consultation is required for a written, personalized quote.
[Schedule a consultation](/request-appointment) and we'll provide a personalized quote for gynecomastia surgery.
Frequently Asked Questions

items: **Is gynecomastia the same as chest fat?** No. True gynecomastia involves glandular breast tissue, while pseudogynecomastia is primarily excess fat. Many patients have a combination, and the distinction affects whether liposuction, excision, or both are appropriate.

**Do I need a medical evaluation before surgery?** Yes. Dr. Hanna will review your health, medications, supplements, substance use, symptoms, and breast development. Testing or another medical evaluation may be recommended when a hormonal condition, medication, or other cause is possible.
**How long does gynecomastia surgery take?** Surgery commonly lasts one to three hours, depending on whether treatment involves liposuction, gland excision, skin removal, or combined techniques.

**Will male breast reduction leave scars?** Every surgical treatment requires incisions. Liposuction scars are small, while gland or skin excision requires longer incisions that are often placed along natural chest contours or the areola border. Scars fade but do not disappear completely.

**When can I return to work and exercise?** Many patients return to desk work within one to two weeks. Heavy lifting, chest workouts, and strenuous exercise are usually restricted for approximately four to six weeks and should resume only after clearance.

**Will I need a compression garment or drains?** A compression garment is commonly used to control swelling and support the new contour. Temporary drains may be needed when more extensive tissue or skin is removed.

**Are the results permanent?** Results are long-lasting in many cases once swelling resolves, but significant weight gain, certain medications or substances, anabolic steroids, or an untreated underlying condition can cause chest enlargement to return.

**Can surgery change nipple sensation?** Temporary numbness or sensitivity changes can occur, and permanent sensation changes are possible. Dr. Hanna will explain how the proposed technique affects this risk.

**Does insurance cover gynecomastia surgery?** Most health plans do not cover cosmetic male breast reduction. Some medically documented cases may be considered, but requirements vary by policy and coverage cannot be guaranteed.

blocks.text: Lip fillers are non-invasive injectable treatments using hyaluronic acid-based substances to add volume, shape, and smoothness to the lips, addressing concerns like thinness, asymmetry, or age-related deflation. This procedure is ideal for individuals seeking to enhance their natural lip features due to genetics, aging, or environmental factors, and it focuses on achieving soft, authentic results that complement facial harmony and boost self-expression, drawing from insights gained through thousands of patients over the years.
**Key Benefits**

items: Natural-looking volume that enhances lip fullness without an overdone appearance.
Smoother contours and diminished wrinkles around the mouth for a refreshed smile.
Quick, customizable enhancements that align with your unique facial aesthetics.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Consultations involve a detailed review of your lip structure, concerns, and goals, often using imaging to preview potential outcomes. The treatment typically lasts 15 to 30 minutes under topical numbing, with precise injections to add volume and shape. Recovery allows immediate return to most activities, with minor swelling or bruising resolving within a few days as final results settle. Costs start around $600 to $900 per syringe, varying based on the amount used and any combined treatments.

*As a board-certified plastic surgeon with decades of experience at Cary Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I have administered lip fillers to thousands of patients, earning multiple "Voted Best Plastic Surgery" awards in the area. This treatment is especially rewarding for those desiring subtle lip enhancement, often transforming smiles by restoring lost volume from aging or creating better balance for naturally thin lips. From my practice, I have observed that many patients achieve the best outcomes when fillers are used conservatively to avoid unnatural "duck lips," and combining with treatments like Botox for perioral wrinkles addresses comprehensive concerns around the mouth.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With over 30 years and thousands of lip filler treatments, I've perfected techniques that deliver soft, natural enhancements without the 'overfilled' look, focusing on symmetry and movement to preserve your authentic smile.

Patients often rave about the confidence boost from subtle volume that feels like their own lips, just better. As a multiple award-winner for Best Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I emphasize your unique lip anatomy and consider shape, proportion, and skin quality for personalized plans that may integrate with other injectables for harmonious facial rejuvenation.
Benefits of Lip Fillers
From my experience, lip fillers do more than add volume—they refine your natural features for a vibrant, expressive smile. Key benefits include:

items: Increased fullness and definition for balanced, youthful lips.
Smoothing of vertical lines around the mouth from aging or habits.
Customizable results that enhance without altering your inherent shape.
Hydration boost from hyaluronic acid for softer, more supple texture.
Quick confidence lift; many patients feel more photogenic and social.
Long-term perks come from maintenance, keeping enhancements fresh.

items: Realistic goals for natural plumping rather than dramatic change.
Good overall health; non-smokers for better healing.

blocks.text: Lip Fillers, Step-by-Step
The treatment is done in-office with topical numbing, lasting 15-30 minutes. Steps include:

items:
**Consultation:**
Discuss goals, assess lips, select filler.

**Preperation:**
Cleanse area, apply numbing cream.

**Injection:**
Precise placement with fine needle for volume/shape.

**Refinement:**
Massage for even distribution.

**Completion:**
Apply ice; provide aftercare tips.

blocks.text: Results appear immediately, refining over days.

Recovery is swift and many patients resume activities immediately, with full settling in days. Based on my protocols:

items: **First 24-48 hours:** Ice to reduce swelling/bruising; avoid strenuous activity, alcohol.
**Week 1:** Gentle lip care; no excessive heat or pressure.
**Beyond:** Hydrate lips; touch-ups as needed.

blocks.text:

blocks.text: Microneedling is a minimally invasive skin rejuvenation treatment that uses fine needles to create controlled micro-perforations in the skin, stimulating the body's natural healing response to produce collagen and elastin. This procedure is ideal for individuals experiencing concerns such as uneven texture, fine lines, acne scars, enlarged pores, or stretch marks due to aging, sun damage, or life changes, and it focuses on achieving gradual, natural improvements that enhance overall skin health and radiance, often transforming confidence based on insights from thousands of patients over the years.

The treatment typically lasts 30 to 60 minutes under topical numbing, with a device creating micro-channels to promote healing. This treatment is highly effective for those seeking to improve skin quality without downtime, often revealing a glowing complexion by addressing accumulated damage from sun exposure or acne. Important aspects I deem essential based on patient outcomes include customizing needle depth to skin type for safety and efficacy, pre-treatment preparation to avoid irritation, and post-care emphasis on sun protection to prevent rebound damage, ensuring progressive, natural skin renewal that lasts.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With over 30 years and thousands of microneedling sessions, I've optimized techniques that maximize collagen without unnecessary aggression, focusing on skin barrier protection to avoid irritation and promote even healing.

Patients often marvel at the gradual glow that emerges, feeling their skin become more resilient over time. As a multiple award-winner for Best Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I prioritize your skin's unique needs and consider skin type, concerns, and tolerance in order to personalize plans that may incorporate serums or combine with other therapies, ensuring safe, effective rejuvenation.

header.sub: Make a Scar Less Noticeable and Better Integrated With the Surrounding Skin
bullets: Improve scar color, texture, contour, or position

Receive a personalized surgical or nonsurgical treatment plan

blocks.text: Scar revision is a group of treatments designed to make a scar less conspicuous and help it blend more naturally with the surrounding skin. Depending on the scar's type, age, location, color, texture, and effect on movement, treatment may involve topical therapy, injections, resurfacing, surgical excision, or a combination of methods.

No treatment can erase a scar completely. The goal is realistic improvement in appearance, comfort, or function while exchanging the existing scar for one that is usually finer, flatter, better positioned, or less noticeable.
**Key Benefits**

items: Improve raised, depressed, widened, discolored, or irregular scars.
Reduce tightness, discomfort, or restricted movement caused by some contracture scars.
Match treatment to the scar with surgical, injectable, resurfacing, or topical options.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Consultation includes the scar's cause and age, prior treatments, symptoms, health history, medications, nicotine use, skin quality, and your goals. Many office or outpatient treatments take approximately 30 minutes to two hours; complex or staged reconstruction can take longer. Anesthesia may range from local anesthesia to intravenous sedation or general anesthesia, depending on the plan. After surgical revision, initial swelling, discoloration, and discomfort commonly improve over one to two weeks, while the scar continues to mature for months. Treatment costs may range from approximately $500 for a limited nonsurgical treatment to $5,000 or more for surgical revision, depending on the scar, technique, anesthesia, and facility needs. A consultation is required for a personalized quote.

*As a board-certified plastic surgeon with more than 30 years of experience at Cary Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I understand that a scar can affect far more than appearance. I evaluate how the scar formed, how it behaves, and whether it affects comfort or movement before recommending treatment. I am honored that this individualized, patient-focused approach has helped our practice earn repeated “Voted Best Plastic Surgery” awards in the area.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With board certification in plastic surgery and more than 30 years of surgical experience, I approach scar revision as a highly individualized problem. I assess scar type, skin tension, location, color, thickness, symptoms, and the original injury or operation before explaining which options are most likely to provide meaningful improvement.

As a repeated Best Plastic Surgery award-winner in Cary, NC, I believe good scar care begins with clear expectations. I will explain the tradeoffs of nonsurgical treatment, resurfacing, excision, and advanced closure techniques, including the possibility that a scar can recur or require staged care. My goal is to create the most refined result the surrounding tissue can safely support—not to promise that a scar can disappear.
Benefits and Candidates for Scar Revision
Scar revision may improve a scar that is raised, depressed, widened, irregular, discolored, painful, itchy, or restrictive. Potential benefits include:

items: A finer, flatter, smoother, or better-positioned scar.
Improved transition between the scar and surrounding skin.
Reduced tightness or improved movement in selected contracture scars.
A treatment plan suited to hypertrophic, keloid, depressed, surface, or contracture scars.
Greater comfort and confidence when a prominent scar is difficult to conceal.

blocks.text: Visit the [American Society of Plastic Surgeons website](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/reconstructive-procedures/scar-revision) for additional information about scar revision.
Ideal Candidates
Scar revision can be considered for a bothersome scar almost anywhere on the body. Good candidates generally:

items: Are physically healthy and have realistic expectations about improvement rather than complete removal.
Do not smoke or are willing to stop nicotine use as directed.
Do not have active acne, infection, or another skin disease in the treatment area.
Have a mature or stable scar, unless earlier treatment is recommended to address function or abnormal scar formation.
Understand that keloids and some hypertrophic scars may recur despite careful treatment.

blocks.text: Scar type matters. Hypertrophic scars remain within the original wound but become thick and raised; keloids can extend beyond it; depressed scars sit below the surrounding skin; and contractures can restrict movement, particularly after burns or across a joint. An examination is needed to determine the appropriate approach.
Scar Revision Treatment Options

rows: Silicone gels or sheets, pressure therapy, steroid injections, and selected fillers may flatten, soften, or support certain scars.
Raised scars, some keloids, or selected depressed scars.
Laser or light therapy, dermabrasion, or chemical peeling can improve color and surface irregularity in appropriate skin and scar types.
Discoloration, uneven texture, or more superficial scars.
The existing scar is removed and the wound is carefully closed in layers to reduce tension and create a finer line.
Wide, irregular, depressed, or poorly positioned scars.
Z-plasty, W-plasty, local flaps, tissue substitutes, or tissue expansion may redirect a scar, release a contracture, or replace deficient tissue.
Contractures, complex scars, burns, or scars that cross natural skin lines.

blocks.text: Scar Revision, Step-by-Step

Scar revision may be performed in the office, an accredited office-based surgical facility, an outpatient facility, or a hospital. The setting, anesthesia, and duration depend on the complexity of treatment.

items: **Anesthesia:** Local anesthesia, intravenous sedation, or general anesthesia is selected for your comfort and safety.
**Scar Treatment or Excision:** The scar may be injected, resurfaced, released, or surgically removed according to the treatment plan.
**Repositioning or Reconstruction:** When necessary, the scar is redirected along natural skin lines or nearby tissue is rearranged to release tension and restore movement.
**Layered Closure:** Deep and superficial tissue layers are closed carefully to support healing and reduce tension at the skin surface.
**Dressing and Aftercare:** A dressing is applied, and you receive instructions for wound care, activity, sun protection, and any topical scar therapy.

blocks.text: Recovery & Aftercare

Recovery varies with treatment depth and location. Following surgical revision, localized swelling, discoloration, and discomfort commonly last one to two weeks. Many patients can resume light daily activity within several days, but work, exercise, lifting, and stretching restrictions depend on the treated area and closure tension.

items: **First several days:** Protect the dressing and incision, use medication as directed, and avoid tension or pressure on the area.
**Weeks 1–2:** Swelling and discoloration begin to improve; sutures may be removed when appropriate.
**Following weeks:** Activity increases gradually while sun protection and recommended silicone or scar care continue.
**Several months to one year:** The revised scar continues to soften, flatten, and fade as it matures.

blocks.text: Contact the office for increasing pain, spreading redness, fever, drainage, wound separation, or another unexpected change. Final results take time, and some scars require additional treatment.
Risks & Complications

Scar revision risks include bleeding, infection, fluid collection, delayed or poor wound healing, skin loss, persistent pain, numbness or other sensation changes, discoloration, prolonged swelling, asymmetry, and an unfavorable or widened new scar. A hypertrophic scar or keloid can return, and additional injections, radiation, pressure therapy, or surgery may be recommended in selected cases.

Anesthesia, blood-clot, cardiac, and pulmonary risks also apply to surgical treatment. Results cannot be guaranteed, and a second procedure may be needed to address recurrence, a complication, or an incomplete improvement. Dr. Hanna will review the risks relevant to your scar, health, skin characteristics, and treatment plan during informed consent.
**Individual results vary.**
Cost & Financing

Scar revision costs vary widely because treatment may range from a limited office procedure to a more complex operation requiring anesthesia and facility time. A practical planning range is approximately $500 for a limited nonsurgical treatment to $5,000 or more for surgical revision. The final fee depends on the scar's size and location, the chosen technique, the number of treatment sessions, and anesthesia or facility needs.

Most health plans do not cover treatment performed only to improve appearance. Coverage may be considered when a scar causes documented functional impairment, but requirements vary and coverage cannot be guaranteed. Financing through CareCredit and major-card payment options are available. A consultation is required for a written, personalized quote.
[Schedule a consultation](/request-appointment) to receive a personalized scar revision treatment plan and cost estimate.
Frequently Asked Questions

items: **Can scar revision remove a scar completely?** No. Scar revision is intended to make a scar less noticeable or improve its function. Every surgical revision creates a new scar, although careful planning may make it finer, flatter, or better positioned.

**When is a scar ready for revision?** Many scars improve as they mature, often over a year or longer. Timing depends on the scar's cause, age, location, symptoms, and behavior. Earlier treatment may be appropriate for a contracture, active keloid, or another functional concern.

**What is the difference between a hypertrophic scar and a keloid?** A hypertrophic scar is raised but stays within the original wound. A keloid grows beyond the original wound and may continue enlarging, itching, or hurting. Keloids have a higher recurrence risk and often require combined treatment.
**How long does scar revision take?** Many office or outpatient procedures take approximately 30 minutes to two hours. Large, complex, or staged reconstructions may take longer.

**What type of anesthesia is used?** Small revisions may require only local anesthesia. More extensive resurfacing, excision, tissue rearrangement, or reconstruction may use intravenous sedation or general anesthesia.

**How long is recovery?** Initial swelling, discoloration, and discomfort after surgical revision generally improve over one to two weeks. Activity restrictions depend on the treated area, and the scar may continue maturing for several months to a year.
**Will I need more than one treatment?** Possibly. Injections, resurfacing, and keloid care commonly require a series of treatments. Complex scars may also be treated in stages.

**Can a revised scar come back?** Yes. Any scar can widen or remain noticeable, and hypertrophic scars and keloids can recur. Following wound-care, activity, sun-protection, and scar-management instructions can support healing but cannot eliminate recurrence risk.

**Does insurance cover scar revision?** Cosmetic scar revision is usually not covered. A plan may consider treatment when a scar causes documented pain, contracture, or functional impairment, but policy requirements vary.

**How much does scar revision cost?** Treatment may range from approximately $500 for a limited nonsurgical treatment to $5,000 or more for surgery. A consultation is needed to determine the technique, setting, and personalized fee.

header.sub: Reshape Prominent Ears for Balanced, Natural Facial Harmony

Performed by award-winning, board-certified plastic surgeon.

blocks.text: Otoplasty, also called ear pinning or ear reshaping surgery, changes the shape, position, or size of the outer ear so it sits in better proportion to the face. This procedure is commonly chosen for ears that project too far from the head, look uneven, or have a misshapen fold. It is performed on the outer ear only and does not affect hearing. The goal is a natural profile that looks balanced from the front and side, based on individualized planning rather than a one-size-fits-all “pinned back” look.
**Key Benefits**

items: Ears that sit closer to the head with a more balanced facial profile.
Correction of prominent, folded, or asymmetrical ear contours.
Greater comfort wearing hair up, glasses, helmets, or hats without self-consciousness.

blocks.text:
**What to Expect**
Consultations include a detailed exam of ear cartilage, projection, symmetry, and your goals. Surgery typically lasts about 1 to 2 hours and is usually outpatient. Incisions are commonly placed behind the ear so scars stay hidden in the natural crease. Recovery often allows a return to school or desk work within about 1 week, with a protective headband worn as directed while swelling settles. A personalized quote is provided at consultation. Costs typically start around $5,000 to $8,000, varying based on whether one or both ears are treated, the technique used, and whether otoplasty is combined with another procedure.

*As a board-certified plastic surgeon with decades of experience at Cary Plastic Surgery in Cary, NC, I have helped thousands of patients with facial and reconstructive procedures, earning multiple "Voted Best Plastic Surgery" awards in the area. Otoplasty is one of the more personal operations I perform, because prominent or uneven ears often affect how someone feels in photos, at school, at work, and in everyday conversation. From my practice, I have seen how a carefully planned setback can restore balance without making the ears look pinned flat against the head.*
Why Choose Dr. Hanna?

With more than 30 years in practice and thousands of procedures performed at Cary Plastic Surgery, I approach otoplasty the same way I approach other facial surgery: natural proportion, hidden scars, and a result that still looks like you.

Patients often tell me they have hidden their ears with hair or hats for years and simply want them to sit closer to the head without looking operated on. As a repeated Best Plastic Surgery award-winner in Cary, NC, I take time in consultation to examine both ears, review photographs, and explain whether the issue is a weak fold, a deep conchal bowl, or both, so the plan is specific to your anatomy rather than a generic “pin back.”
Benefits of Ear Surgery
Otoplasty is designed to improve how the ears sit relative to the face. Common benefits include:

items: Ears that project less from the side of the head and look more proportionate in photos and profile.
Better symmetry when one ear sits differently than the other.
Correction of a weak or missing antihelical fold that makes an ear look prominent.
Hidden scars placed in the crease behind the ear in most cases.
Greater ease wearing hair up, shorter styles, glasses, or helmets.

blocks.text: *Otoplasty addresses the outer ear only. Hearing is not changed by this operation.*
Visit the [American Society of Plastic Surgeons website](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/cosmetic-procedures/ear-surgery) for complete information on Otoplasty surgery.
Ideal Candidates

Ideal candidates are healthy children, teens, or adults who are bothered by ear position, size, or shape and have realistic goals. Ears are typically near adult size around age 5 to 6, which is why many surgeons consider that the earliest common age for elective otoplasty. Good candidates often have:

items: Ears that project farther from the head than they prefer.
Asymmetry between the two ears.
A weak or absent antihelical fold, a deep conchal bowl, or both.
Stable health, no active ear infection, and the ability to follow aftercare, including headband use.

blocks.text: Adults who have lived with prominent ears for years are also common candidates. Patients with bleeding disorders, poor wound healing, or unrealistic expectations of “ears glued to the head” are not ideal. The goal is a natural setback, not an overly flattened look.
Technique Options

rows: Permanent sutures recreate or strengthen the antihelical fold. Scarring is hidden behind the ear.
Sutures set the conchal bowl closer to the mastoid. This reduces projection at the base of the ear. Scars are hidden behind the ear.
Cartilage is weakened or a small amount is reduced so it holds a new shape. This is helpful when sutures alone are not enough.
Firmer adult cartilage or excess conchal cartilage.
Mix of the above, sometimes with skin adjustment. Each ear can be planned independently and scars can typically be hidden behind the ear.
Asymmetry, prior surgery, or mixed anatomy.

blocks.text: Ear Surgery, Step-by-Step
Otoplasty is usually an outpatient procedure and commonly lasts 1 to 2 hours. Steps include:

items: **Anesthesia:** General anesthesia or local anesthesia with sedation, chosen based on age and comfort.
**Incision:** A cut is made behind the ear, in the natural crease where the ear meets the head.
**Cartilage work:** The antihelical fold is created or strengthened, the conchal bowl is set back if needed, and extra cartilage or skin is reduced only when necessary.
**Internal support:** Long-lasting sutures hold the new shape.
**Closure and dressing:** The incision is closed and a protective dressing is applied.

blocks.text: Outpatient procedure. You will go home the same day with aftercare instructions.
Recovery & Aftercare
Most patients return to school or desk work in 1 to 2 weeks. Contact sports are often delayed until about 6 weeks, depending on healing. Typical aftercare includes:

items: **The first several days:** Keep the head elevated, protect the dressing, and take prescribed pain medicine as directed. Do not sleep on the operated ear.
**After the first dressing change:** Wear a soft headband as instructed, often full-time at first and then at night only, so the ear is not folded forward in sleep.

**Weeks 2 to 4:** Swelling and bruising continue to fade. Avoid heavy glasses, pressure, helmets, and contact sports until cleared. Longer term: Scars behind the ear typically fade over months. Protect healing skin from sun.

blocks.text: **Tips:** Button-down shirts are easier than pullovers at first. Avoid rubbing or bending the ear. Call the office for increasing pain, spreading redness, fever, or a sudden change in ear position.
Risks & Complications

Otoplasty is a well-established outpatient procedure, but every surgery has risks. These include bleeding, infection, reaction to anesthesia, visible or thickened scarring, asymmetry, overcorrection or undercorrection, suture irritation, numbness, and the possibility of revision. Cartilage can try to return toward its original shape, which is one reason sutures and aftercare matter. We review your health history in consultation so you can decide with full information.
**** Individual results vary**
Cost & Financing

We will always provide transparent pricing with no hidden costs. Otoplasty (ear) surgery typically starts at $5,000 and includes anesthesia, facility time, and follow-ups. Pricing varies depending on the techniques required, if only one ear is treated vs. both, and combinations with other surgeries.
We offer financing through CareCredit and accept major cards. During consultation, get a custom quote; insurance may cover if medically necessary.
[Schedule a consultation](/request-appointment) and we'll provide you with a personalized quote for otoplasty surgery.
Frequently Asked Questions

items: **How long does otoplasty surgery take?** Otoplasty usually lasts about 1 to 2 hours at our practice, depending on whether one or both ears are treated and how much cartilage work is required.
**Will otoplasty leave visible scars?** Most incisions are placed in the crease behind the ear, so scars are usually hidden from the front view and fade over time.

**Will insurance cover my otoplasty procedure?** Cosmetic setback of prominent ears is often not covered. Coverage is more likely to be considered when there is a reconstructive indication. The office can help you understand what documentation, if any, is needed.

**How long do the results of otoplasty last?** Once the cartilage heals in the new position, results are generally long-lasting. Aging does not typically reverse a well-performed setback, though trauma or poor aftercare can affect an early result.
**Does otoplasty affect hearing?** No. Otoplasty is performed on the outer ear and does not change the middle or inner ear structures that produce hearing.

blocks.text: About Dr. Hanna

Dr. Donald Hanna is a distinguished board-certified plastic surgeon who has dedicated his career to helping patients achieve their aesthetic and functional goals with natural, beautiful results. Based in Cary, NC, he founded Cary Plastic Surgery to provide a welcoming environment where advanced techniques meet compassionate care.

With over 30 years in the field and thousands of successful procedures, Dr. Hanna is known for his meticulous attention to detail and commitment to patient satisfaction. His practice encompasses a wide range of services, from breast enhancements and body contouring to facial rejuvenation and non-invasive treatments, all tailored to enhance your unique beauty.
Professional Background and Education

Dr. Donald P. Hanna brings an exceptionally strong foundation in medicine and surgery to his practice at Cary Plastic Surgery. After completing his undergraduate studies in microbiology at the University of Michigan, he earned his medical degree from Wayne State University School of Medicine. He then completed a rigorous five-year general surgery residency at the State University of New York Downstate Medical Center, followed by advanced fellowship training in plastic surgery at Duke University Medical Center. During this period, he also served as the Christine Kleinert Fellow in Hand Surgery at the University of Louisville, gaining specialized expertise in microsurgery and reconstructive techniques.
Dr. Hanna’s academic and professional credentials include:

items: **Board Certification:** Double board-certified by the American Board of Plastic Surgery and the American Board of General Surgery
**Licensure:** Licensed to practice medicine in North Carolina and Michigan

**Academic Appointments:** Served as Clinical Assistant Instructor in the Department of Surgery at SUNY Downstate Medical Center and as Instructor in the Division of Plastic, Reconstructive, and Maxillofacial Surgery at Duke University Medical Center
**Specialized Training:** Completed advanced courses in basic and advanced microsurgery

**Research and Scholarship:** Authored peer-reviewed publications and book chapters on topics including free vascularized joint transfers and perioperative antibiotic use in hand surgery; presented at national meetings of the American Society for Surgery of the Hand

blocks.text: This extensive training and ongoing commitment to surgical excellence allow Dr. Hanna to deliver the highest standard of care, combining technical precision with an artistic eye for natural results.
Areas of Expertise

Dr. Hanna excels in a variety of plastic surgery procedures, drawing from his extensive experience to deliver personalized results. His expertise includes [breast augmentation](/breast-plastic-surgery/breast-augmentation), [lifts](/breast-plastic-surgery/breast-lift), and [reductions](/breast-plastic-surgery/breast-reduction) for harmonious enhancements; body contouring like [tummy tucks](/body-plastic-surgery/tummy-tuck), [liposuction](/body-plastic-surgery/liposuction), and [arm lifts](/body-plastic-surgery/arm-lift) to sculpt and refine; facial rejuvenation through [facelifts](/face-plastic-surgery/facelift), [rhinoplasty](/face-plastic-surgery/rhinoplasty), and [blepharoplasty](/face-plastic-surgery/blepharoplasty) for youthful vitality; and non-invasive options such as [lip fillers](/cosmetic-plastic-surgery/lip-filler), [injectables](/cosmetic-plastic-surgery/injectables), and [microneedling](/cosmetic-plastic-surgery/microneedling) for subtle refreshes.
He is particularly noted for his approach to natural-looking results, using advanced techniques to minimize scarring and downtime while maximizing patient comfort and satisfaction.
Philosophy of Care
Dr. Hanna's philosophy is rooted in the belief that plastic surgery should empower patients to feel confident in their own skin, emphasizing natural results over dramatic changes.
He approaches each case with empathy, listening closely to your goals and concerns to create a customized plan that respects your anatomy and lifestyle.

Safety is paramount, with rigorous protocols and state-of-the-art technology ensuring optimal outcomes. This patient-centered ethos extends to every team member, fostering a supportive environment where education and transparency build trust from the first consultation to final follow-up.
What Our Patients Are Saying
Awards and Recognition

Dr. Hanna has been honored with multiple 'Voted Best Plastic Surgery' awards in the Cary area, reflecting the trust and high regard of both patients and peers. Additional recognitions include serving as President of the Aesculapian Society during medical school and holding numerous leadership positions at local hospitals, such as Division Chief of Plastic Surgery at Rex Hospital (1999–2005), Chair and Vice-Chair of the Department of Surgery at WakeMed Cary Hospital, and multiple terms as President-Elect of the Medical Staff. These roles demonstrate his longstanding commitment to clinical excellence and medical leadership in the community.

Voted BEST Plastic Surgery
in Cary, North Carolina for 7 Years!
Personal Touch and Community Involvement

Beyond his professional achievements, Dr. Hanna is deeply committed to the Cary community, participating in local health initiatives and educational seminars to promote informed choices in plastic surgery. He has also given back through tutoring roles in chemistry, algebra, biochemistry, and English across various locations, including the University of Michigan, Nigeria, and Paris. This personal touch ensures that every interaction feels genuine and supportive, creating a practice environment where patients feel like valued individuals rather than just cases.

blocks.text: Our Philosophy and Approach

At Cary Plastic Surgery, our philosophy centers on delivering natural, beautiful results that enhance your confidence and align with your lifestyle. We believe in a patient-first approach, where every treatment is customized to your anatomy, goals, and concerns.

Safety is paramount, with rigorous protocols to minimize risks and ensure optimal outcomes. From the initial consultation to follow-up care, we prioritize open communication, empathy, and education, empowering you to make informed decisions.
This commitment stems from years of seeing how personalized care transforms lives, fostering long-term relationships built on trust.
Expertise and Experience

Led by board-certified Dr. Donald Hanna, our practice brings decades of specialized experience in plastic surgery, having helped thousands of patients achieve their aesthetic visions. Our team stays at the forefront of advancements through ongoing training and use of proven techniques, ensuring precise, effective treatments.

Patients appreciate our focus on natural results, avoiding overdone looks while addressing specific needs like volume restoration or contour refinement. This expertise not only delivers beautiful outcomes but also minimizes complications, with a track record of high satisfaction from real patient stories.
Awards and Recognition
Cary Plastic Surgery has been honored with multiple 'Voted Best Plastic Surgery' awards in the area, reflecting our dedication to excellence and patient satisfaction.

These recognitions from peers and community highlight our consistent delivery of outstanding results and service. While awards are gratifying, our true measure of success is the positive impact on our patients' lives, as seen in their stories and feedback.

Patient-Centered Care

We put patients at the heart of everything, offering friendly, knowledgeable staff who guide you through every step with compassion. From detailed consultations that address your questions to customized aftercare plans, we ensure you feel heard and supported. Our focus on transparency includes clear explanations of procedures, risks, and recovery, helping you prepare fully. This approach has built lasting trust, with many patients returning for additional treatments or referring loved ones, knowing they'll receive the same exceptional care.

State-of-the-Art Facility

Our modern plastic surgery practice in Cary, NC, is designed with your comfort and safety in mind. The welcoming foyer sets a calming tone from the moment you arrive, while our accredited operating room is equipped with advanced technology for precise, hygienic procedures.

We adhere to the highest standards of cleanliness and innovation, creating an environment that feels like a sanctuary rather than a clinic. This setup allows for seamless care, from consultations to recovery, ensuring every visit is positive and stress-free.
